To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Millennium Project in the country is not relevant to the local context, and that it does not provide an appropriate indicator of sustainable development in Nepal.
the MDG 2015 targets and indicators for Nepal do not adequately represent Nepal’s development context and are not sufficient to ensure equitable development.

MDGs are not context specific, they are not comprehensive enough to capture the complexity of development, they do not reflect inequality and they do not capture the ecological sustainability of development.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: 1) Are the MDGs relevant for Nepal? 2) Do the MDGs provide an adequate context for sustainable development? 3) What are the gaps in the MDGs for Nepal? 4) What are the implications of the MDGs for sustainable development in Nepal?
the relevance and comprehenses of Millennium Development Goals for Nepal and the extent to which they reflect the country’s sustainable development needs.
the following: (i) the Millennium Project in its entirety, (ii) its relevance and comprehensivenss for Nepal, and (iii) its relevance and applicability for the Nepalese people
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Millennium Development Goals have been a failure in Nepal, and the Millennium Project in the country is not relevant.
, although the MDG 8 (global partnership for development) has been partially met in Nepal, the country has failed to achieve the MDG 1-7.
Nepal’s progress towards the MDG 8 has been slow, but the country has met most of its MDG 7 targets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MDG framework is not appropriate for Nepal and other developing countries.
the MDGs are not adequate to capture the complex and dynamic nature of sustainable development in Nepal.
the MDG 8 is not a suitable framework for Nepal, as it does not capture the complexity of development conditions in Nepal, and it does not reflect the needs of all Nepali people.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a more comprehensive, inclusive, and context-specific approach to development is required for sustainable development.
a more comprehensive, inclusive, and contextually relevant framework is needed to ensure that the development goals and indicators are truly sustainable.
the MDGs were not designed for Nepal.
